title: Atom Builders: On Your Own
subject: physical science
instructions: Answer on your own, even though you built atoms with your group. Use a periodic table. Write your ID number, not your name.

questions.skill: I can find protons, neutrons, and electrons
questions.prompt: Inside the Atom: Fill in the missing numbers.
questions.notes: Mass number = protons + neutrons. Charge = protons − electrons, so 8 − 10 = −2. Look for 26 for the oxygen ion's mass number (electrons counted) and +2 (sign flipped).

questions.skill: I can explain what decides the element
questions.prompt: Change One: Which change makes an atom a different element?

options.why: That makes an ion of the same element.
That makes another isotope of the same element.
Yes: the number of protons decides the element.
That makes a positive ion, still the same element.

questions.skill: I can find protons, neutrons, and electrons
questions.prompt: Mass Number: A student says an atom with 6 protons, 6 neutrons, and 6 electrons has a mass number of 18. What's the mistake?

options.why: Electrons have almost no mass; they aren't counted.

options.text: The mass number counts only protons and neutrons, so it's 12.
The mass number counts only protons, so it's 6.
options.why: That's the atomic number; neutrons count too.

options.text: The mass number counts only neutrons, so it's 6.
options.why: Protons count in the mass number too.

questions.skill: I can explain what decides the element
questions.prompt: Same Element? Carbon-12 and carbon-13 are both carbon. Explain why, and say what's different about them.
questions.key: Both have 6 protons, and the number of protons decides the element; carbon-13 has one more neutron (7, not 6), so its mass number is higher. Full credit needs both: same protons, so same element, and a different number of neutrons. Either one alone is partial.

questions.skill: I can find protons, neutrons, and electrons
questions.prompt: Draw It: Draw a lithium-7 atom. Put protons and neutrons in the nucleus (the small circle) and electrons outside it. Mark protons +, neutrons n, and electrons −.

diagram.description: An empty frame with a circle (the nucleus, about 70 points across) in the middle.

checklist.item: Exactly 3 protons (marked + or p) are inside the small circle.
Exactly 4 neutrons (marked n or 0) are inside the small circle.
Exactly 3 electrons (marked − or e) are outside the small circle.
